facts.statement: The genus Ruehleia was established by Galton in 2001.
The type species R. bedheimensis was named in honor of the German paleontologist Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern.
facts.quote: The type species is R. bedheimensis, described by Galton in 2001, and is named for the German paleontologist Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern.

facts.statement: The holotype of Ruehleia was discovered in 1952.
facts.quote: Discovered in 1952, the holotype consists of one nearly complete skeleton

facts.statement: Fossils of Ruehleia were found in the Trossingen Formation in central Germany.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in the Trossingen Formation of central Germany

facts.statement: Ruehleia lived during the Norian stage, approximately 216 to 208 million years ago.
facts.quote: date to the Norian stage, around 216 to 208 million years ago

facts.statement: Ruehleia belongs to the family Plateosauridae.
Ruehleia is classified within the class Saurischia.
The time range for Ruehleia is estimated between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
